A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same conditional scaling-law and architecture-search work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training experiments, scaling-law fits, downstream evaluations, inference measurements, and architectural ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds hardware/serving-system evaluations and WikiText perplexity comparisons with released checkpoints.

M1.justification: The conditional calibration formulas, constrained architecture search, local GQA search, and selected Panda/Surefire architectures remain unchanged. Appendix I expands documentation of the existing GQA experiment without establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds WikiText language-modeling evaluation in Appendix H, Tables 7–8. Dolma-v1.7 training and the original nine downstream benchmarks remain unchanged, making this a limited extension of dataset coverage.

E2.justification: New Tables 7–8 substantially broaden comparisons beyond the retrained LLaMA architectural baselines: they additionally evaluate LLaMA-3.2-1B-HF, OLMo-2-1B-HF, LLaMA-3.2-3B-HF, and Qwen2.5-3B-HF. These released-checkpoint comparisons are distinct from the retained controlled comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 extends throughput evaluation from A100/vLLM to A100/SGLang and H200 with both frameworks. Appendix H adds byte-level WikiText perplexity and checkpoint comparisons at batch size 128, including a 2048-input/1024-output setting accommodating OLMo. The original training protocol and hyperparameters are retained.

E4.justification: Appendices F–G add substantial portability tests of Surefire versus LLaMA across hardware and serving systems, plus Qwen3 architectural sensitivity sweeps on H200. The original outlier, calibration, fitting-data, GQA-loss, and MoE analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify throughput averaged over five repeated runs. v2's detailed throughput table adds point estimates without introducing confidence intervals, significance tests, additional seed information, or a changed uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Original training losses, downstream accuracies, and plotted results are retained. v2 adds extensive throughput and WikiText results; Table 6 reports 12645.55 versus 8608.57 tokens/s for Surefire-1B versus LLaMA-3.2-1B on H200/SGLang at batch 128, approximately 47% higher throughput. This concerns an added setting, not an improvement to a retained measurement.

T1.justification: The scaling-law equations, separability assumption, constrained optimization, and FLOPs derivation are unchanged, including v1 Appendix H becoming v2 Appendix K. The expanded GQA discussion adds mechanistic intuition rather than a new formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract retains the same architecture-aware scaling-law and search contributions, model-scale scope, and headline accuracy/throughput gains. The expanded conclusion restates the existing search procedure and cites additional comparisons as supporting evidence.

C2.justification: v2 adds a proposed query/KV-capacity explanation for fluctuating GQA losses, interprets cross-platform transfer, and discusses released-model architectural tradeoffs. Section 7 removes v1's limitation that different architectures might require different hyperparameters.

D1.justification: v2 documents hardware, serving frameworks, and input lengths for the added evaluations, and explains the fixed total-head budget in the existing GQA sweep. Architecture and training-hyperparameter listings are retained. The reproducibility statement removes the promise to release configuration files and scripts; actual resource availability is not established.

R1.justification: v2 adds Bian's 2026 architecture-design thesis and Voita et al. (2019) on attention-head specialization. Most existing related-work discussion is retained in Appendix B, and the positioning against earlier scaling-law approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact. Local revisions move three related-work discussions into Appendix B, expand the GQA explanation and conclusion, revise captions and subsection wording, and add acknowledgements and the conference header.

P2.justification: v2 adds a front-page throughput/loss contour visualization, nine additional inference figures, and three tables covering throughput and checkpoint comparisons. Existing figures are retained with renumbering, caption edits, and some relocation, producing a substantial expansion of the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The added hardware/serving-system tests strengthen v1's narrow A100/vLLM validation, while WikiText and released-checkpoint comparisons improve empirical context. Reporting weaknesses limit the gain: the new claim of superiority across all settings conflicts with Table 6, where Surefire-3B achieves 2542.21 versus LLaMA's 2593.04 tokens/s on H200/SGLang at batch 16. v2 also removes the architecture-dependent hyperparameter caveat and the promised script/configuration release.
